concept.name: Transaction count
concept.definition: Transaction count is the total number of successful on-chain transactions over a period — the basic measure of how much settlement activity a blockchain processes.
concept.intuition: It is the number of checks the ledger cleared today, regardless of their size.
concept.mechanics: Glassnode defines the metric as the total number of successful transactions per interval (hour/day); it reflects demand for block space but not economic weight, since a $10 payment and a $100M transfer each count once. Fee levels, mempool congestion and batching practices all interact with raw counts.
concept.failure_modes: Counts are trivially inflated by spam, inscription-style data embedding or self-transfers, so raw transaction count is a weak measure of economic activity — CDD and transfer-value metrics exist partly to fix this; exchange batching suppresses counts even as volume grows.
concept.misconceptions: More transactions do not mean more adoption or more value moved — bot activity and dust spam inflate counts. Compare value-weighted or age-weighted metrics before drawing conclusions.
concept.example: Bitcoin processes on the order of 500,000-650,000 successful transactions per day; during inscription booms, counts spiked sharply while transfer value stayed flat — activity up, economic throughput unchanged.
